text:
alex: Heads-up — the sample-app's paginator + client-side throttling is causing duplicate page fetches when auth retries kick in. Repro on local with small windowing settings.

mira: ugh. do you have a minimal repro? is it the js sdk or go? :eyes:

alex: js SDK. repro steps: set concurrency=3, pageSize=50, enable clientThrottle and set burst=10. Hit endpoint with mocked 401s on token refresh. After retry we end up fetching the same page twice (sometimes 3x).

priya: can you paste the snippet? curious whether the retry is requeuing the same cursor or creating a new one.

alex: snippet: `for await (const page of paginator()) { await send(page) }` then our retry middleware does `if (is401) await refreshToken(); retryRequest(req)`. The retry doesn't attach the current cursor header so server treats it as a fresh request -> duplicate.

sam: hmm that sounds like a race between token refresh and the batching/queue. If the throttle buffer reorders requests, the retry might not preserve the original request meta. We saw something similar with backpressure in the sampleapp last quarter.

mira: +1. possible fixes: (1) make retry wrapper clone and preserve `x-pagination-cursor` header, (2) make throttle queue pin request IDs so retries map to original slot, or (3) expose a retry hook in SDK to mutate original request rather than create a new one.

alex: i tried option (1) quickly — preserving cursor header fixes duplicates but causes a failing assertion on the server when seq numbers mismatch (server expects monotonic seq). So we need to ensure the retry replays the same logical page request, not just header.

priya: could we make the SDK attach a retry-token id and server dedupe on that? similar to idempotency keys. lightweight and helps other retry cases too.

sam: that feels clean. add `x-sdk-retry-id: <uuid>` on first attempt and propagate on retry. Server checks if it already processed that retry-id for that client+cursor. fallback: short TTL cache.

alex: i'll sketch a quick PR for js-sdk with `retry-id` approach. will add integration test that simulates token refresh during throttle-induced reorder.

mira: awesome. can you link the branch when ready? we should also add an example to the sample-app so onboarding users don't trip over this.

alex: yup — will do. tagging the ops bot to run the integration on CI.

ops-bot: CI run queued for job sample-app/integration/retry-throttle (build 4821) :white_check_mark:

priya: thank you! adding to the SDK parity checklist — mirror change in go and python clients.

mira: filed a tiny doc note in devex-runbook about "Retries + pagination" with mitigation patterns. linking after PR. :thumbsup:

alex: cool, thanks team. will follow up with PR link later.
